import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import norm, t, skewnorm

# ---- Editable priors for the 6 strategies (family + parameters) ----
strategies = [
    {"title": "Analytics / GameMgmt: Optimal 4th-down aggression",
     "family": "normal", "params": {"mu": 0.72, "sigma": 0.3673},
     "most_plausible": 0.72},
    {"title": "Analytics / Offense: Expand play-action usage",
     "family": "skew_normal", "params": {"xi": 0.14, "omega": 0.80, "alpha": 4.0},
     "most_plausible": 0.48},
    {"title": "Analytics / Defense: Two-high light-box base",
     "family": "normal", "params": {"mu": 0.38, "sigma": 0.4082},
     "most_plausible": 0.38},
    {"title": "Intuition / GameMgmt: Proactive end-of-half timeouts",
     "family": "normal", "params": {"mu": 0.18, "sigma": 0.3469},
     "most_plausible": 0.18},
    {"title": "Intuition / Offense: No-huddle tempo as base",
     "family": "student_t", "params": {"nu": 4, "mu": 0.28, "sigma": 0.5764},
     "most_plausible": 0.28},
    {"title": "Intuition / Defense: Manufacture takeaways",
     "family": "student_t", "params": {"nu": 4, "mu": 0.32, "sigma": 0.4683},
     "most_plausible": 0.32},
]

def make_dist(s):
    f, p = s["family"], s["params"]
    if f == "normal":
        return norm(loc=p["mu"], scale=p["sigma"])
    if f == "student_t":
        return t(df=p["nu"], loc=p["mu"], scale=p["sigma"])
    if f == "skew_normal":
        return skewnorm(a=p["alpha"], loc=p["xi"], scale=p["omega"])
    raise ValueError("unknown family: " + f)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(16, 9))
axes = axes.ravel()

for ax, s in zip(axes, strategies):
    dist = make_dist(s)
    lo, hi = dist.ppf(0.025), dist.ppf(0.975)
    span = hi - lo
    xs = np.linspace(lo - 0.5 * span, hi + 0.5 * span, 600)
    pdf = dist.pdf(xs)
    ax.plot(xs, pdf, lw=2, color="navy")
    mask = (xs >= lo) & (xs <= hi)
    ax.fill_between(xs[mask], pdf[mask], alpha=0.25, color="navy",
                    label="95%% interval [%.2f, %.2f]" % (lo, hi))
    mp = s["most_plausible"]
    ax.axvline(mp, color="crimson", ls="--", lw=1.5,
               label="most-plausible = %.2f" % mp)
    ax.axvline(0.0, color="gray", ls=":", lw=1)
    ax.set_title(s["title"], fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlabel("Change in own scoring margin (points)")
    ax.set_ylabel("density")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper right")
    print(s["title"])
    print("  family:", s["family"], "| params:", s["params"])
    print("  ppf 95%% interval: [%.3f, %.3f]" % (lo, hi))
    print()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

quantity.description: Change in own-team expected single-game scoring margin (own points − opponent points) from adopting the strategy versus not, holding everything else equal; an average per-game effect.
quantity.support: unbounded real; positive favors own team

prior.consistency_check: 0.72 lies inside [0.0, 1.44]; normal support is all of R, covering signed (including negative) values.

distribution_family.justification: The underlying models are well-validated and replicated, so both sign and magnitude are fairly pinned down; the effect is unlikely to land far from center, so symmetric with moderate tails fits.
distribution_family.name: normal

parameters.conversion_note: Normal: mu = most_plausible = 0.72; sigma = (high - low)/3.92 = (1.44 - 0.00)/3.92 = 0.3673. Interval is symmetric about mu by construction.

strategies.rationale: Win-probability and expected-points models repeatedly show conventional coaches forfeit fractions of a win per season by punting/kicking in go situations; converting those decisions adds expected points and shortens the opponent's field, which maps directly onto wins.
strategies.recommendation: Adopt a model-driven 4th-down policy: go for it on essentially all 4th-and-1s past our own 30 and on 4th-and-short in opponent four-down territory, and keep the punt/FG unit off the field in spots WP/EP models flag as negative-EP.
strategies.title: Optimal 4th-down aggression

prior.consistency_check: 0.48 lies inside [-0.1, 1.8]; skew_normal support is all of R, covering signed values.

distribution_family.justification: Asymmetric belief: a floor near zero because defenses adapt and surprise decays, but a longer upside tail with the right personnel/scheme, so right skew is appropriate.
distribution_family.name: skew_normal

parameters.conversion_note: Skew-normal, right skew via alpha = +4 (skewness ~0.78, Gaussian-decaying tails). Fit numerically: using standard SN(alpha=4) mode ~0.42 and standard quantiles q.025 ~ -0.28, q.975 ~ 2.10, solved omega ~0.80 and xi ~0.14 so the mode ~0.48 and central 95% ~[-0.08, 1.82], approximately the stated [-0.1, 1.8]. Approximate; the script's ppf prints the exact interval.

strategies.rationale: Public charting shows play-action carries a sizable EPA/dropback premium that is largely independent of run-game success, yet most offenses use it well below the efficiency-maximizing rate; more PA means more explosive, lower-risk completions, which lift scoring margin.
strategies.recommendation: Roughly double our play-action rate, especially on early downs and outside obvious passing situations, and keep using it even when the base run game is mediocre; pair it with boots/keepers to stress second-level defenders.
strategies.title: Expand play-action usage

prior.consistency_check: 0.38 lies inside [-0.42, 1.18]; the interval crosses zero, honestly reflecting backfire risk; normal support covers signed values.

distribution_family.justification: A bounded structural tilt with genuine two-sided risk (against heavy-run teams or with poor tackling it can backfire) and no strong skew or fat-tail mechanism.
distribution_family.name: normal

strategies.rationale: Explosive plays (especially 20+ yard passes) are the strongest per-play driver of scoring drives, and analytics shows trading low-EPA rushing yards to deny high-EPA explosives is a favorable exchange many staffs still resist.
strategies.recommendation: Default to two-high safety structures with lighter boxes on early downs to take away explosive passes and force methodical drives, conceding efficient-but-low-value rushing yards; vary coverages within the two-high umbrella rather than reverting to single-high to stuff the run.
strategies.title: Two-high light-box as base

prior.consistency_check: 0.18 lies inside [-0.5, 0.86]; interval is wide relative to its small center and dips clearly negative, reflecting honest low confidence; normal support covers signed values.

distribution_family.justification: A small, two-sided effect with no fat-tail mechanism; the real downside (spent timeouts unavailable if the script flips, and the opponent also benefits from a stopped clock) is captured by a wide-relative-to-center symmetric spread.
distribution_family.name: normal

strategies.rationale: Intuition basis: public models quantify offensive in-possession clock/timeout use but rarely isolate the value of spending DEFENSIVE timeouts to manufacture a pre-half possession or the before/after-half 'double.' Winning link: an extra expected possession per half is worth real points, and the deferred second-half kickoff compounds it. This is one of my weaker picks and the prior reflects that.
strategies.recommendation: When we have deferred, use defensive timeouts aggressively in the last ~3-4 minutes of the second quarter to force a punt and get the ball back with time to score before half, chasing the two-possession swing of scoring just before and just after intermission, rather than hoarding timeouts.
strategies.title: Proactive end-of-half defensive timeouts (the double-up)

prior.consistency_check: 0.28 lies inside [-1.32, 1.88]; student_t support is all of R; heavy tails put real mass on both large positive and large negative effects.

distribution_family.justification: Genuinely two-sided with potential for large swings either way (snowball upside vs. gassed-defense / short-field downside), so symmetric center but heavy tails.
distribution_family.name: student_t

strategies.rationale: Intuition basis: public analytics on sustained tempo is genuinely mixed—more snaps help us but also the opponent, and rest our defense less—so there is no clean consensus effect. Winning link: constraining the defense's personnel and pressure menu can raise our per-play efficiency and force mistakes, and the effect compounds when it snowballs.
strategies.recommendation: Operate primarily from no-huddle tempo by default (not just in two-minute) to lock the defense into base personnel, limit exotic pressures and disguise, and prevent specialized substitutions, accepting fewer huddles and a faster game clock.
strategies.title: No-huddle tempo as a base operating mode

prior.consistency_check: 0.32 lies inside [-0.98, 1.62]; student_t support is all of R; interval reaches well into negative territory, reflecting the tackling tradeoff and luck component.

distribution_family.justification: Turnovers are extremely high-variance and high-leverage, so a non-trivial chance of a large |effect| in either direction is essential—heavy tails, modest positive center.
distribution_family.name: student_t

strategies.rationale: Intuition basis: analytics treats turnovers as high-leverage but largely luck-driven (fumble recovery, INT variance), so it is skeptical that emphasis reliably creates them. Winning link: takeaways are among the biggest EP swings in football (short fields, lost possessions, occasional return scores), so even a small, noisy bump buys points—though the tackling tradeoff adds genuine downside.
strategies.recommendation: Drill aggressive ball disruption—second-defender punch-outs, rake-throughs, and attacking the catch point—as a weekly point of emphasis, accepting a marginally higher missed-tackle/YAC risk in exchange for more forced fumbles and contested-throw takeaways.
strategies.title: Manufacture takeaways via ball-disruption coaching
